tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description specifies concrete trigger conditions (CheckPatchingPrerequisites Failed, bare exit status 1 with compliant instance, PingStatus ConnectionLost/Inactive, TimedOut/DeliveryTimedOut) and uses 'Use when...' imperative phrasing. It focuses on the operational scenarios the user faces rather than internal mechanics, and while dense, it stays within a reasonable paragraph length given the complexity of the triage domain it must disambiguate.
tests.evidence: Use when the CheckPatchingPrerequisites automation reports Failed, a patch operation returns a bare "failed to run commands: exit status 1" while the instance is already compliant, an instance shows PingStatus ConnectionLost/Inactive, or a run reports TimedOut/DeliveryTimedOut.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is tight and domain-specific throughout — no explanation of general concepts like what EC2 or SSM are. Every sentence conveys non-obvious triage logic specific to this patch workflow.
tests.evidence: Precheck failures have dependencies — fix the right thing first. If connectivity (S3/IMDS/credentials) or UpdateServiceConfigurationStatus (repo/subscription health) is failing, fix those first

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large reference tables or API docs are embedded in the body; detailed material is consistently delegated to reference/ files linked conditionally per case, keeping the body to triage logic and short rules.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, high-stakes operations (auto-closing OpsItems, deregistering hybrid instances) get exact prescriptive gates, while flexible remediation (timeout fixes: split/parallelize/pre-stage/lengthen) is presented as options with rationale rather than a single rigid path.
tests.evidence: only auto-close a failure when a fresh scan proves FailedCount=0 and MissingCount=0 ... Split security-first, enable parallel downloads, pre-stage packages, or lengthen the window

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple remediation options are listed for timeouts, they are presented as a flexible menu appropriate to the task (window-sizing has no single correct fix), and other decision points (e.g., which reference file to read) are deterministic classifications, not tool choices needing a default.
tests.evidence: Split security-first, enable parallel downloads, pre-stage packages, or lengthen the window

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable triage procedure (classify case, run gates, follow ordered recovery, validate) applicable to any instance/run facing these four situations, not a one-off instance-specific declaration.
tests.evidence: Step 1: Classify the triage case: a precheck reported Failed → ... a bare failure but instance looks compliant → ... PingStatus not Online ... TimedOut / window exceeded

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: A dedicated Gotchas section lists concrete, non-obvious environment-specific corrections (WMI corruption masking disk-space errors, hybrid ghost handling, compliance gate before closing) that the agent would likely get wrong otherwise.
tests.evidence: Windows disk-space failure is often WMI corruption — winmgmt /verifyrepository before expanding a volume.

tests.reasoning: This is primarily a triage/decision-support skill rather than a report-generation skill; it does reference evidence-backed resolution notes but doesn't require a heavy structured report template, and the validation section already specifies what evidence must appear in close notes.
tests.evidence: an OpsItem was only resolved after a fresh scan proved FailedCount=0 && MissingCount=0 with the resolution note citing that evidence

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: A dedicated Validation section instructs the agent to check its own conclusions (fresh re-run pass, compliance gate proof, exclusion vs deregistration, cleared interrupted state) before finalizing, and explicitly says to re-classify if checks fail.
tests.evidence: If any check fails, re-classify — don't auto-close a real failure or treat an unreachable ghost as patchable.
